What I did: PR 680 is open at https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/680. It is on the right repo, mergeable,
and not merged. My commit f82d83013 added only ob-442/T4.txt.
What went wrong: While the monitor ran, someone pushed commit 87b99fdd6 to the branch, authored by ryan@ironbelly.com
and titled "ob-442 O-10 edit". It adds a second line, ob-442 o10 edit, to the file. The PR head is now that commit,
not mine, so the monitor's head check (pr_head_mismatch) fails.
Reviews:
- Codex: clean. It reviewed my commit f82d83013, which is before the new push.
- Augment: one Medium finding on the new head. It says the file should hold only ob-442 T4, and the second line breaks
that.
Why I stopped: Augment's finding is correct against issue 679. But the extra line looks like a deliberate edit for
another observation (O-10), not a mistake. Fixing it would mean reverting someone else's commit on my own authority.
The monitor was also not allowed to push on a moved head. No fix was applied, nothing else was pushed, no review
thread was replied to or resolved, and the PR is still open and not a draft.
My recommendation: Keep the second line if O-10 needs it, and ignore Augment's finding. If you want the file to match
the issue, remove it. Either way, the checkout in this worktree is one commit behind the branch.
- Keep: I leave the PR as it is. Nothing changes.
- Remove: you tell me to, and I fetch the branch, delete the second line, push one fix commit, and resume the monitor.
